articles.title: Lunar Eclipse Event & Details
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting a lunar eclipse viewing party and general meeting on November 8th at Houge Park, featuring a barbeque, observation of the total lunar eclipse, and talks by Bob Garfinkle and Jane Houston Jones. The article provides detailed eclipse timing information, observing tips for the challenging moonrise during totality, and a comprehensive calendar of other SJAA activities for November and December 2003.

articles.title: Slide and equipment night, September 2003
articles.summary: The September 2003 Slide and Equipment night featured Gary Mitchell's experiment on dark adaptation, suggesting light color is less important than intensity, and Mark Wagner's demonstration of an innovative collapsible Dobsonian rocker box. Attendees also learned about a budget-friendly 2-inch eyepiece from Anacortes, making the event a showcase of practical astronomical innovations and equipment.

articles.title: Address (e and postal) and phone number updates
articles.summary: This article reports on recent activities and administrative updates for an astronomy organization, likely SJAA. It highlights Akkana Peck's "Mars season" presentation, which included maps, an applet, and an inflatable globe, and details a "slide and equipment night" where members showcased various astronomical projects and gear, such as a green laser pointer, a wooden refractor pier, and a collapsible Dobsonian base. The document also includes a request for members to update their contact information.

articles.title: Shoot the Moon
articles.summary: Inspired by another amateur's work and a new digital camera, author Dave North, previously a non-photographer, successfully attempts Moon astrophotography. He details an easy method using a Canon Elph camera and a telescope eyepiece, emphasizing that good results are achievable without expensive equipment or extensive effort. This personal experiment sparked a wave of similar "cheapo" Moon photo attempts among other enthusiasts, proving the accessibility of the hobby.

articles.title: Another moonrise eclipse
articles.summary: The article provides an astronomy observing guide for November, detailing optimal viewing conditions and features for Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune, and Venus. It highlights specific insights into Mars' shrinking south polar cap, potential dust storms, and north polar hazes, while also announcing a moonrise lunar eclipse on November 8.

articles.title: The shallow sky
articles.summary: This article discusses the challenging visibility of a deep partial lunar eclipse on November 8th, offering tips for observation despite its occurrence during twilight. It also announces the SJAA Fall Astronomical Swap Meet on November 9th, detailing items for sale, logistical information, and expected vendors. Additionally, the San Jose Astronomical Association is selling 2004 RASC Observer Handbooks and calendars as a fundraiser for its equipment loaner program.

articles.title: Celestial calendar November 2003
articles.summary: This article presents a comprehensive celestial calendar for November 2003, detailing lunar phases, planetary positions (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn), hours of darkness, and sidereal time. It also announces two key astronomy events in the San Francisco Bay Area: a farewell gathering for the Morrison Planetarium on November 19th, marking its closure after 50 years, and a public lecture on 'The Mystery of Black Holes' by Dr. Alan Dressler on November 12th.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article outlines the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) telescope loaner program, providing details for members interested in borrowing equipment. It lists telescopes that are immediately available, those currently on loan with due dates, scopes with extended loan periods, and a waiting list for various models. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to inquire about borrowing a telescope or to be placed on a waiting list.
